title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono meet Andy Warhol | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono met the artist Andy Warhol on 6 June 1971.

The couple went to Warhol’s exhibition at the Whitney Museum in New York City, after which they went with him to the New York Flea Market, held each Sunday at 25th and 6th in Manhattan. Afterwards they went to The Factory, Warhol’s studio at 33 Union Square West, and the Museum of Modern Art at 11 West 53rd Street.

Later on in the day, Lennon and Ono were introduced to musician Frank Zappa at the Mayfair Hotel. Zappa was doing an interview with radio reporter Howard Smith, who had been acting as Lennon and Ono’s New York guide since their arrival.

Smith brought the couple to Zappa’s hotel room, not informing the singer beforehand. Zappa invited them into his room, and asked them to jam with The Mothers of Invention that night at the Fillmore East.

Following their meeting with Zappa, Lennon and Ono watched David Peel and The Lower East Side perform at Washington Square Park, before going to the Fillmore East to play with Zappa.
